title: Sliding puzzles
description: A sliding puzzle's start/goal shapes and the starts and goals stamped on them (decision 0014; the original's Start/Goal tab). A start/goal shape is a tray: its empty cells are walls, its variable cells corridors a piece may cross but not stop on (both edited with shape.setCells); each piece may have a start and a goal on it for each copy the problem has, the whole piece at a time; any copy may end on any of its goals, and the copies without a start start anywhere, those without a goal end anywhere. Trays and pieces may be more than one layer deep: a stamp marks every cell of its piece, and on a tray of several layers a piece may also move up and down as it slides when the solve allows it (SlidingOptions.verticalMoves). The start/goal shapes (boards, labelled B1, B2, ...) stay above the pieces in the list and are numbered 1, 2, ... by place, renumbered when one is deleted or moved. The problems are the user's (problem.create), each with a board chosen as its result (problem.setResult; the original gave each board a problem of its own); several may share a board, each with starts and goals of its own (they are the problem's, not the board's: the sliding.* calls take the problem, and without one mean the board's first; a board no problem uses has none, and the calls that change them are refused, invalid_argument). An edit of a board (shape.setCells, shape.resize, shape.task) takes the starts and goals of its problems along with its cells: one whose cells are all still floor stays, where they now are, one that lost a cell is removed whole, with a notice; a problem given another board (problem.setResult) keeps those that fit it at the same cells. A problem on a board keeps the pieces it has stamped as parts and its colour locks follow them; no board is a piece of any problem; the shape commands keep the stamps in step (shape.delete, shape.move, shape.duplicate, shape.rename, and an edit that changes a piece's shape takes its stamps off). A problem with a start for every piece can also be played by hand (decision 0039): sliding.playStart, sliding.playReach and sliding.playReplay answer what a position allows by the search's rules and keep no game, and sliding.setLayout makes a position the problem's starts or goals. Refused (unsupported) on other grids.

sliding.addStartGoal.summary: Adds a start/goal shape (the original's New Start/Goal) of 'size' cells (default 6 by 6 by 1, the original took the selected shape's; a size [x, y] is one layer), all floor, numbered after the others. No problem is made for it: a problem chooses it as its result (problem.setResult).

sliding.place.summary: The start/goal editor's click: the whole of a piece as its start (goal false) or its goal, placed from a click on cell 'at' (y rises upwards, as in the grid editor): the piece's slice on that layer with its top-left cell there, at the lowest height that puts a layer of the piece on that layer and fits (on a tray of one layer, the piece's top-left cell there). A piece the problem has one copy of moves there if it was elsewhere; one of several copies is one more copy's start or goal, beside the others, refused once every copy has one; a copy that is exactly there already is taken off. Refused (invalid_argument) with the reason when it does not fit: off the floor, on another piece's or another copy's start or goal, a goal on a corridor, every copy placed. The problem loses what it had found. One undo step.

problem.description: The problem shown, whose result must be this board (refused otherwise, invalid_argument): the starts and goals are its own, its counts the copies. Without it, the board's first problem.

placed.description: The piece is there now (false: it was there and was taken off).

sliding.clearAt.summary: Takes off a problem's start or goal of the copy that covers a cell (the editor's right click), not the piece's other copies. One undo step; nothing when none covers it.

problem.description: The problem whose starts and goals these are, whose result must be this board (refused otherwise, invalid_argument). Without it, the board's first problem.

sliding.clone.summary: Copies every start a problem has on its start/goal shape onto its goals (toGoal true), or every goal onto its starts, replacing what that side had (the Puzzle workspace's Clone start to goal and Clone goal to start). Refused (invalid_argument) with the reason when a start is on a variable cell (a goal cannot be on one). The problem loses what it had found. One undo step.

problem.description: The problem whose starts and goals these are, whose result must be this board (refused otherwise, invalid_argument). Without it, the board's first problem.

sliding.clear.summary: Takes every start (goal false) or every goal a problem has off its start/goal shape (the Puzzle workspace's Clear Start position board and Clear Goal position board); cleared is false, and nothing changes, when that side had none. The problem loses what it had found. One undo step.

problem.description: The problem whose starts and goals these are, whose result must be this board (refused otherwise, invalid_argument). Without it, the board's first problem.

sliding.tray.summary: What a start/goal shape holds for a problem: its number and name, each cell's start and goal (the piece stamped there, cells indexed x + X*(y + Y*z)), each copy placed with its cells, whether it can be solved (the validity bar: null, or why not: starts or goals that are not whole pieces, more of them than the problem has copies, or no piece with every copy at a start and at a goal), the stamps larger than their pieces' copies (null, or the message), and its floor cells.

problem.description: The problem shown, whose result must be this board (refused otherwise, invalid_argument): the starts and goals are its own, its counts the copies. Without it, the board's first problem.

name.description: The user's part of its name; the board shows it, or 'Board n' while it is empty.

placed.description: Each copy of a piece placed, at a start (goal false) or a goal, its cells sorted lowest layer first, top row first, left to right; marks that are not whole pieces come as one entry.

sliding.preview.summary: Where sliding.place would put a piece: the cells, every layer (when no height fits, the lowest that puts a layer of the piece on the layer of 'at'; none when no layer of the piece can be there), whether it fits (and the original's reason when not), and whether a copy is exactly there already (then the click takes it off). Changes nothing.

problem.description: The problem shown, whose result must be this board (refused otherwise, invalid_argument): the starts and goals are its own, its counts the copies. Without it, the board's first problem.

sliding.gridAdvice.summary: Whether optimized paths would narrow a sliding problem's search (decision 0029), from its board and the starts and goals stamped: the largest grid that divides the board's floor, whose cells some piece (a block) measures a multiple of and on whose lines every such piece starts and fills its goals, and that leaves fewer stops; with it, every piece stops only where pieces of its cells start or fill a goal, or where it fits in a block's hole. The Solver asks before a solve whether to use it (SlidingOptions.optimizedPaths). Changes nothing.

grid.description: Cells a side; 0 when the board fits no such grid (or the problem has no board or no starts), and optimized paths would search every stop.

stops.description: The places the problem's pieces can stop on the empty board, summed over the pieces (each copy counted); 0 without a grid.

gridStops.description: Those the grid leaves (fewer than stops); 0 without a grid.

sliding.resumeAdvice.summary: Whether solve.continue with these options would carry a paused sliding solve's saved search on from the start alone where solve.start would search from the start and from the goal until the two meet (decision 0033), which is far faster: a search with nested slides and optimized paths that a version before the two ends saved. Such a search is carried on as it was begun, so the Solver asks before Continue whether to solve again from the start instead. Changes nothing.

fromStartAlone.description: True when a start the paused solve keeps for its next run has a search saved in slideFolder that goes on from the start alone, and a new search of it would go from both ends. False otherwise: nothing paused or saved, a search saved from both ends, a problem that is searched from the start alone anyway (a piece that may end anywhere, partly nested pieces), other options (no nested slides, no grid), and while the problem's run is active.

sliding.playStart.summary: How a game of a problem played by hand starts (decision 0039): its board, its pieces where its starts put them, and its goals. The pieces are in the order a solve numbers them (the problem's parts in order, copy by copy; the copies of a piece in the order sliding.tray lists their starts), and the play calls name a piece by its place in this list. A piece is placed by the lowest corner of its cells on the board (the least x, y and z of a cell it fills), which does not change when the piece is redrawn in its grid or a solve moves its hotspot; a position is such a cell for each piece. A problem that cannot be played is no error of the call: 'error' says why (its result is no board, it has no pieces, a start is not a whole piece, a piece has starts for fewer or more than its copies) and there are no pieces. Changes nothing.

error.description: Why the problem cannot be played; null when it can.

cells.description: The floor: every cell that is no wall; a variable cell is a corridor, which a piece may cross and rest on, but no position with a piece on one is solved.

board.description: The problem's board (its result, a start/goal shape); null when its result is none.

at.description: Where it starts: the lowest corner of its cells.

cells.description: The cells it fills, from that corner (none negative).

origin.description: That corner in the shape's own grid: a cell [x, y, z] of 'cells' is the shape's cell origin + [x, y, z]. It places the shape's picture (ShapeImage.box, in the grid's cells) on the piece.

goals.description: Each goal stamped, a whole piece, with its board cells (goals that are not whole pieces are left out).

hasGoal.description: The problem has goals; without any, no position is solved.

solved.description: The start is the goal already.

sliding.playReach.summary: Where one move can take a piece of a position, by the slide search's rules: one move is the piece going anywhere it can reach while the others stay put, round corners included, in its layer unless 'rules' allows vertical moves. The groups are those the search moves: the piece alone; with nested slides also the piece with what is nested in its outline (when anything is); with partial nesting also the wider group (when it is wider). Each stop says whether the position it gives is the goal, as the search judges it (any copy of a piece on any of its goals, a piece without a goal anywhere, no piece resting on a variable cell; never when the problem has no goals). The stops of a group are joined by single steps to the place it is at: a drag follows them. Refused (invalid_argument) with the reason when 'places' is no position of the problem's pieces on its board (another number of places, a piece off the floor, two on one cell) or there is no such piece. Changes nothing.

piece.description: The piece, by its place in sliding.playStart's list.

movers.description: The piece first, then what it carries.

stops.description: Every shift the group can reach in one move, nearest first; none when it cannot move.

sliding.playReplay.summary: Makes a list of moves one after another from a position, and tells each one's route: what checks moves read from a file, plays moves back, and checks them again after the problem changed. A move is the pieces that move as one (a group sliding.playReach gives for one of them, in any order) and their shift, which must be one they can reach. Each step has the corner points of the move's route as shifts from where the pieces were, start and end included, with the fewest straight runs (as a solution's moves are drawn), and whether the position after it is the goal. It stops at the first move that cannot be made: 'illegal' is its place in the list and 'why' the reason, and 'steps' has the moves before it. With no moves it tells whether the position is the goal. Refused (invalid_argument) with the reason when 'places' is no position of the problem's pieces. Changes nothing.

solved.description: The position the moves start from is the goal.

illegal.description: The first move that cannot be made (from 0); null when all were.

sliding.setLayout.summary: Makes a position a problem's starts (goal false) or its goals, replacing what that side had: every piece marked where the position puts it (the Play workspace's Save position as Start and as Goal). Refused (invalid_argument) with the reason when 'places' is no position of the problem's pieces on its board, or a goal would be on a variable cell. 'changed' is false, and nothing changes, when that side is the position already; otherwise the problem loses what it had found. One undo step.

PlayPlaces.description: A position of a problem's pieces: for each piece of sliding.playStart's list, the lowest corner of its cells on the board.

SlideShift.description: A shift [dx, dy, dz] in cells.

movers.description: The pieces that move as one, by their places in sliding.playStart's list.

PlayMove.description: One move of a game played by hand.

nestedSlides.description: A piece may carry what is nested in its outline.

partialNested.description: And what is partly nested in it; implies nestedSlides.

verticalMoves.description: On a board more than one layer deep, a piece may also move up and down.

PlayRules.description: The rules of a game that the problem does not fix, each off when left out: SlidingOptions' of the same names. The engine does not read the problem's stored solver settings for them.

TrayCell.description: A cell [x, y, z] of a start/goal shape, y up; [x, y] is on its first layer (z = 0).

TraySize.description: A size [x, y, z] in cells; [x, y] is one layer.
